subject: dec
title: (R)DEC.------DYM.F.
description: Diagram in MID-W-16. (R)DEC (the reality of decentralization) is crossed with DYM-F (dynamic functionalism). The pairing is structurally pointed: real decentralization (not the concept) crossed with dynamic functionalism asks what actual decentralization *does* when it operates as a dynamic-functional principle (rather than a political slogan). DYM-F → DEC (the crossing). LK-IMP (linkage implications) → INFO-CON (information convergence) → PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) → TR (transformation). INFO-CON → DYM-SPT (dynamic spiritualism) → MTA-RT-SIGN (meta-reality significance). (P)TM (the point of activation of terminology) → MTA-RT-SIGN. DYM-F → MTA-RT-SIGN. Structural argument: real decentralization arrives via dynamic functionalism. The parallel productive chain runs through linkage implications → information convergence, which fans into progressional continuance → transformation *and* dynamic spiritualism → meta-reality significance. Meta-reality significance is the central convergence point — fed by *three* upstreams (dynamic spiritualism, the point-of-activation of terminology, and dynamic functionalism). The diagram thus diagrams the structural conditions for what makes a decentralized organization actually meaningful: it requires that linkage implications connect to information convergence (collective communication of meaning), which then bifurcates into both progressional-continuance-leading-to-transformation *and* dynamic-spiritualism-leading-to-meta-reality-significance. The AACM diagrammed: it survives only as long as both arms remain active.
